data.name: Opaline
data.detailed_description:
Storyline



Gallow is a young boy that nothing pre-destined to become a True Knight, one of the world's most treasured titles. When he is summoned by the Crusaders and forced to leave his village of Hermon, the pain of losing a friend is too hard for Liza to endure, and she can't resist the urge to secretly follow him. But when a legendary monster attacks them both at night, she realizes that she, like Gallow, may also have more in her than meets the eye. Can the two of them have what it takes to preserve the world from the rise of the Blight?
Play Opaline and discover what awaits Gallow and Liza!

Features



* Visible monsters and mouse control
* Play two split parties with their own characters and inventory
* Find numerous Secret Rooms in dungeons
* Explore and collect up to 14 relics
* Help people on your way and complete the many sidequests the game has to offer
* Pick one mode among three (easy-normal-hard) to fit your playing style - an Aldorlea signature
* Discover Gallow and Liza's destiny - can they end up together when their fates seem to pull them apart?

Similar Games

  • Asguaard
  • Moonchild
  • Girlfriend Rescue
  • The Tale of a Common Man
  • Undefeated

data.short_description: In this 16-bit style RPG, Gallow and Liza are two teenagers gifted with great powers, and that destiny seems to persist in keeping away from each other, however their feelings drive them close. Can the two of them have what it takes to preserve the world from the rise of the Blight?

reviews.review:
Opaline, developed by Warfare Studios and published by Aldorlea Games, is a fantasy RPG that proudly embraces the traditions of classic Japanese role-playing games. Built using RPG Maker, the title presents an adventure that values storytelling, character relationships, and exploration over mechanical complexity. From the outset, it establishes a familiar setup: a peaceful life interrupted by forces beyond human understanding. While the premise may not immediately distinguish itself from countless fantasy RPGs before it, the game gradually reveals that its greatest strength lies in the journey shared by its central characters rather than in its overarching conflict.

The story revolves around Gallow and Liza, two young companions whose lives are forever altered when Gallow is summoned to pursue the prestigious path of becoming a True Knight. What begins as a simple coming-of-age tale evolves into a larger struggle involving ancient corruption known as the Blight. Rather than focusing solely on heroic deeds and epic battles, Opaline spends considerable time exploring the bond between its protagonists. Their separate experiences and eventual reunions provide the narrative with an emotional core that helps distinguish it from more generic fantasy adventures. Although some plot developments are predictable, the sincerity of the writing keeps the experience engaging throughout its lengthy campaign.

A notable aspect of the game is its use of dual protagonists. Players regularly switch between Gallow and Liza, each leading their own party and experiencing different parts of the world. This structure adds welcome variety and gives players multiple perspectives on the unfolding events. It also allows supporting characters to receive more attention, creating a broader sense of scale than one might expect from an RPG Maker title. The alternating storylines are handled effectively and help maintain interest during quieter stretches of the narrative.

Gameplay remains firmly rooted in traditional turn-based RPG design. Battles are straightforward, relying on standard attacks, skills, and party management rather than innovative mechanics. Enemy encounters are visible on the map, which gives players more control over exploration and removes the frustration associated with random encounters. The game also includes multiple difficulty settings, making it accessible to newcomers while still offering a reasonable challenge for veterans. Hidden areas, optional quests, and collectible relics encourage thorough exploration, rewarding players who take the time to investigate every town, dungeon, and side path.

Visually, Opaline captures the atmosphere of retro console RPGs with colorful environments and sprite-based characters. Its presentation is modest, but it succeeds in delivering a nostalgic charm that aligns perfectly with its design philosophy. Character portraits add personality during conversations, while the soundtrack complements both the lighter moments and the more dramatic scenes. However, limitations associated with RPG Maker are evident throughout the adventure. Environmental assets occasionally feel repetitive, and dungeon layouts can become formulaic over time. These shortcomings do not ruin the experience, but they do reinforce the game's identity as a smaller-scale production.

What ultimately makes Opaline memorable is its commitment to delivering a heartfelt adventure without overextending its ambitions. It does not attempt to revolutionize the genre or impress players with technical spectacle. Instead, it offers a comfortable and familiar experience built around friendship, romance, and heroism. Fans of retro-inspired RPGs will appreciate its emphasis on exploration and narrative, while players seeking deeper combat systems or groundbreaking ideas may find it somewhat conventional.

Despite its occasional pacing issues and reliance on established fantasy tropes, Opaline remains an enjoyable and sincere role-playing experience. Warfare Studios and Aldorlea Games have crafted a title that understands exactly what it wants to be: a nostalgic journey that recalls the era of classic JRPGs while adding enough personality to stand on its own. For players looking for an old-school adventure filled with charming characters and a sense of discovery, Opaline offers many hours of satisfying entertainment.

Rating: 6/10
